text: This is a thousand metres down. The sun has never shone here. So how is anything alive?
Some animals skip eyes, like these shrimp on underwater volcanoes, where the vents top four hundred degrees.
Almost three thousand metres. The deepest any mammal has dived: Cuvier's beaked whale. It's held its breath for over three hours.
Three thousand eight hundred. The Titanic, at three hundred and eighty times surface pressure. Yet fangtooth, hagfish and dumbo octopus live here.
Six thousand. The hadal zone. The trenches.
Eight thousand three hundred. The deepest fish ever filmed, a little snailfish.
Tip Everest in, and its summit stops here. Still not the bottom.
In 1960, Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh reached Challenger Deep, almost eleven thousand metres down. Director James Cameron went solo in 2012.
Robots followed. Japan's Kaiko collected three hundred and fifty species. And since 2019, over twenty people have touched the bottom.
Yet we've explored just five to ten percent of the ocean.
So next time you're at the beach, maybe don't look down.
